svg.aria-label: Classification of dyes by method of application
svg.title: Classification of dyes by method of application
svg.desc: Table-tree of acid, basic, direct, mordant, vat, sulphur, azoic, disperse and reactive dyes with fibres, mechanism and examples
svg.text: Classification of dyes by method of application
Nine main classes; each class matches the chemistry of the fibre it dyes
How the dye is held / applied
Neutral bath + NaCl / Na₂SO₄; long planar molecule
held by H-bonds and van der Waals forces
Fibre + metal ion (Al, Cr, Fe, Sn) + dye →
insoluble coloured chelate (lake) in the fibre
Insoluble dye reduced (Na₂S₂O₄ + NaOH) to soluble
leuco form, absorbed, re-oxidised by air
oxidised on the fibre; polysulphide dyes
Fibre soaked in naphthol, then treated with diazonium
salt at 0–5 °C: dye is formed on the fibre
Fine aqueous dispersion; dye dissolves in the fibre as
a solid solution (high temperature or carrier)
Dye reacts with –OH / –NH₂ of the fibre in alkaline
Also: solvent dyes (plastics, inks, fuels), ingrain dyes, pigment dyeing and food dyes.
